I will still farm the way I know, starting from what worked before, not chasing fancy changes. On my 4.1 mu, I will keep more land in cotton because cotton is still the main cash crop for me, and I have well water, so I can hold it steady if the weather turns dry. I will put 2.1 mu into cotton, 1 mu into millet, and 1 mu into mungbean. With my age and only 2 people in the house, I will not make the field plan too scattered or too labor-heavy. I finished middle school, so I do look at input and yield together. Cotton eats more fertilizer and spray money, but if I cut too hard and lose bolls, that hurts more than spending a bit extra. Millet and mungbean I will manage more tightly on cost. Mungbean itself can help the soil a bit, so I will not push nitrogen hard there. Millet I will keep simple, mostly one basal application and one good watering if needed. I will use improved seed where I have seen good results nearby. I do not blindly change everything, but if a variety has done well in nearby fields for a few years, I will use it.
